transcript.text: Thanks, Marcus. I think assigning the moderated remote question-and-vote channel to a specific role rather than rotating is the right call — clear accountability is exactly what was missing in those sessions where no one was watching the chat. I'd lean toward creating a dedicated 'remote participation coordinator' role rather than folding it into the deputy chair's responsibilities, and here's why: during the transition term, the deputy chair will likely be taking on a lot of new responsibilities, and I don't want remote participation to become a secondary duty that gets deprioritized again. A dedicated role sends a clear signal that remote member participation is a priority, and it ensures someone is always focused on that channel during sessions. That said, if we go with a dedicated role, we'd need to think about how that person is selected and whether it's a formal position in the charter or a designated assignment each cycle. On the transition structure more broadly, I think the 90-day term should include a clear midpoint check-in with Elena to assess how things are going and whether any adjustments are needed before the term ends. That way we're not waiting until day 90 to evaluate whether the structure is working. Elena, does a dedicated remote participation coordinator role seem like something you'd want formalized in the charter, and would you want to define how that role gets filled as part of this process?
